visible_action_claim: A single connected box-derived form is first Bevel-modified with Limit Method None, then altered with loop cuts and demonstrated with Angle limiting, before Vertex Group selection is shown as an explicit hand-authored alternative.
spoken_reason_claim: The instructor distinguishes indiscriminate None limiting from geometric Angle limiting and from hand-selected Weight or Vertex Group limiting; the modifier remains non-destructive.

frame_observations.observed_fact: The Bevel modifier has just been introduced on a simple box form before the limit-method comparison begins.
The now-varied single mesh is visibly evaluated with Angle selected in the Bevel modifier, while the parameter panel exposes the limit-mode choices.
Vertex Group is visibly selected as the explicit hand-authored Bevel-limiting alternative after the Angle example.

transcript_segments.text: The limit method is the threshold for when the modifier should bevel. None indiscriminately bevels every edge loop or vertex.
Angle can limit the modifier to corners exceeding a chosen angle, demonstrated after adding more varied shape.
Weight and vertex groups hand-pick corners, and the Bevel modifier remains non-destructive over later edits.

transcription_provenance.limitations: Machine text was checked against visible modifier-state frames and must not be treated as a creator-authored quotation.

claim_boundary: This verifies one source episode's visible/speech alignment. It does not prove that Angle or Weight is universally correct for a production asset.
